cases.name: disable-then-write-captures-nothing
cases.notes: §5.9 (Phase 4a): capture on from the repository's birth — `a.md` is captured under `c_0`/`r_0` (one revision, one commit, dispositions, the recorder's holds `3`). `history disable` at 10:01 closes the interval (`{ from: <birth>, to: 10:01 }`, `writer_requires` 0). Everything after it is the core's alone: the edit of `a.md` (`c_1`, head `r_1`), the new `b.md` (`c_2`, `r_2`) and the observed deletion of `b.md` (`c_3`) write feed rows and entries, move heads, pool the deleted blocks and claim every id with the core's bit only (`holders 1`) — no `commits`, `revisions`, `dispositions` or `block_changes` row appears after `c_0`, `blobs`/`tree_nodes` hold the first revision alone, and `read_at` of the current head `r_1` finds no recorder row (`target_missing` at the store level; the surface serves the current head from the rows, resolution 11). The sweep at expiry removes the pooled block. The feed is dense `1..4` while the log holds `seq 1` only (H4 within coverage).

cases.name: born-disabled-then-enable-writes-the-baseline
cases.notes: §5.9 (Phase 4a; contracts §1.14): a repository created with capture off (`capabilities: { history: false }` — what a core-only build or `omg source add --no-history` does: `disabled`, no coverage, `writer_requires` 0). Two documents are observed and one edited uncaptured (`c_0`–`c_2`; no history table exists yet). `history enable` at 10:10 executes the bundle's DDL and writes the BASELINE: one feed row `c_3` (`origin import`, `reason 'history enabled'`, its own batch) with a `changed` entry per live document under its EXISTING head (`r_1`, `r_2` — nothing is minted), the `commits` row, and a checkpoint `revisions` row per live document (`seq 1`, the current tree and frontmatter from the rows, `rendered_hash = file_hash`, `commit_id = c_3`); the recorder's hold lands on every live doc, head and block (`holders 3`), the uncaptured `r_0` stays the core's alone (`1`). The manifest opens `{ from: 10:10, to: null }` with `writer_requires` 1. The next edit (`c_4`) is captured as `seq 2` — a delta against the baseline. A second `history enable` changes nothing (`changed: false`, no second baseline). `read_at` reads the baseline's checkpoint revisions (`r_2` of `d_0`, `r_1` of `d_1`) back byte for byte; the uncaptured `r_0` has no row.

cases.name: disable-enable-reconciles-the-edge-record
cases.notes: §5.9 (Phase 4a): the baseline reconciles the recorder's edge intervals with the open edges (H6). Captured: `a.md` links `b.md` (`e_0` opened at `c_0`). Capture off: the link moves to `c.md` — the core deletes `e_0` and opens `e_1` with no transition written. `history enable` closes the dangling `e_0` transition at the baseline commit `c_3` and opens `e_1` from it; the open set and the record agree again (the runner's H6). A disabled `history disable` is a no-op (`changed: false`).

cases.name: recorder-fault-rolls-the-member-back
cases.notes: §5.4 step 15 (Phase 4a; resolution 18): capture runs inside the member's transaction, so a recorder that throws rolls the member back. `a.md` lands (`c_0`). With the fault on, a batch of two — the edit of `a.md` and the new `b.md` — commits nothing: both outcomes are `failed` (the error names the path), the feed still ends at `seq 1`, `a.md` keeps `r_0`, no `b.md` row exists, no pool row, no claim beyond `c_0`'s; the `capture_failed` alert is raised (advisory under A1). With the fault off the same batch lands as `c_1`/`c_2` and the alert about each path clears. The fixture device `recorder_fault` is the runner's (README §9.4); the production path it exercises is `observeBatch`'s per-member catch. The ids the rolled-back members minted (`c_1`, `c_2`, `b_2`–`b_4`) are consumed — the minter is a process counter, a rollback does not return an id — so the landed batch is `c_3`/`c_4` with `b_5`–`b_7`; nothing claims the consumed ids.

steps.error: history capture of a.md failed: recorder fault (fixture device) — the write was rolled back and is retried by the next sweep; fix the recorder or run omg history disable
